Title: Wakey, Fast Reaction, and replacmement oddity.

Messages.Author: L. Scott Johnson
Messages.Body:
Situation:

I have a blocker (B) about to enter combat.
I have a tapped vampire (V) with auspex.
I have a Wakey and Fast Reaction in my hand.

B and the acting minion play out their combat.
I play Wakey and Fast Reaction on V, who now enters combat.
I do not replace the Wakey until the new combat is over.

---
But, if I had played the Wakey at the start of B's combat
(still playing it on V, of course), I would have
replaced it at the end of the first combat, and had an
extra card in hand available during the entire second combat.

---
Just something to think about.

First, how long does the duration of a Wakey last? I mean, can this vamp
do his (her) do for the remainder of the turn? I allways thought it
counted until the action on which it was played was either blocked or
succesfull. In this case you're scenario wouldn't work out, as the action
was allready blocked. In your example, I see you play the card as usefull
until combat is over and resolved (how about a FoM, would it still count
as well?).
Second, somehow I have the feeling that the *combat* in *do not
replace until...* means combat for V. However, this again starts a new
interesting question: what if you use Wakey to block an action, but you
fail to do so? Would this mean you couldn't replace the card until
a) One of your vamps has been in combat
b) This vamp has been in combat
c) Until it is certain the blocking doesn't succeed.

We both would choose c), because it is more logical. But by this same
logic, you can only replace the Wakey until after V's combat.

Wakey lasts for the duration of the action. Fast Reaction is played
within that timeframe.

>Second, somehow I have the feeling that the *combat* in *do not
>replace until...* means combat for V. However, this again starts a new
>interesting question: what if you use Wakey to block an action, but you
>fail to do so? Would this mean you couldn't replace the card until
>a) One of your vamps has been in combat
>b) This vamp has been in combat
>c) Until it is certain the blocking doesn't succeed.

>We both would choose c), because it is more logical. But by this same
>logic, you can only replace the Wakey until after V's combat.

All "Do Not Replace Until After Combat" cards are replaced at the
end of the next combat, or at the end of the action, whichever comes
first. Who is engaged in combat is irrelevant. (So none of the above
are actually official).

Sure, and I agree with your viewpoint - that wakey cannot be replaced
until after its usefulness has passed. But I was merely echoing the
official stance on all "DNRUAC" cards. My own view of how the cards
should work is often in conflict with the official view. I was pointing
out this timing oddity as an example of how strange things can get under
the official rules.

Officially, you may wake and block and, if the opposing vampire continues
the action with superior Form of Mist, play more intercept (+1) and block
again - because the wake is still in effect. You'd replace the wake at the
end of the first combat, however, per card text.

Is that an official ruling ?
It sounds a bit off and is obviously leading to such weird situations
as you outlined above.

Lets view it from a different perspektive:
"Do Not Replace..." is mostly found on non-skill cards, punishing you
for not using a skill based card.
A ruling like "replaced at the end of the NEXT combat" would get rid
of that punishment and I'd consider that a bug.

I agree it might be difficult to find a general ruling that is free
of contradiction.

What would be the drawback if "Do Not Replace..." cards were replaced
after the playing minion finished his next combat or the current action
is finished ? (Which IMHO is how it was meant to be anyway)

Messages.Author: Thomas R Wylie
Messages.Body:
At the end of each combat (and after each action), replace any "do not replace
until after combat" cards that have been played since the last end of combat.
If a card such as Fast Reaction is used to generate another combat, you still
replace cards at the end of the original combat.
